source_text:
τρεφόμενοι ὅλας ἐν αὐτοῖς χωροῦσι τὰς Μούσας, καὶ εἴποις ἂν ἀκούων ὡς ἄνθρωποί
τε ἦσαν καὶ γεγόνασι τέττιγες". Οὐκοῦν στέργειν τοῖς παροῦσιν εἰκός, κἂν οἱ
πράκτορες ἐνοχλῶσιν, ᾆδε μόνον αὐτοῖς, καὶ τῶν χρημάτων εὐθὺς ἐπιλήσονται.
thought_title: Cicadas, contentment, and song against tax collectors
orientation: Procopius is closing his playful letter, still quoting the imagined speech of Dionysus about the poor man devoted to the Muses, and then turns to direct advice for the addressee.
pass_a_gloss: Feeding, they contain within themselves the whole Muses, and you would say, hearing, that they were both humans and have become cicadas. Therefore it is fitting to be content with present things, and even if the tax collectors are troubling, only sing to them, and they will immediately forget about the money.

lemmas.gloss: to be content with, to love

choices.term: ὅλας ἐν αὐτοῖς χωροῦσι τὰς Μούσας
choices.english: they contain within themselves the whole Muses
choices.why: Keeps the literal force of χωρέω as 'contain/hold within' and the plural 'Muses' with 'whole' modifying them, preserving the image of the cicadas as vessels of the Muses.
rejected: they hold all the Muses inside themselves
the Muses wholly dwell in them

choices.why: Renders the potential optative with ἂν and the circumstantial participle literally, keeping the second-person generalizing address.
rejected: you might say when you hear

choices.english: it is fitting to be content with present things
choices.why: στέργειν means to be content with or accept, and τοῖς παροῦσιν is a standard idiom for present circumstances; 'fitting' renders εἰκός.
rejected: one should love what is present
it is reasonable to accept the present

choices.english: and even if the tax collectors are troubling
choices.why: κἂν is 'and even if' with subjunctive, and ἐνοχλέω means to trouble or harass; keeps the concessive force.
rejected: even though the tax collectors bother
and if the tax collectors annoy

choices.why: Keeps the imperative force of ᾆδε and the limiting μόνον, with the dative of person addressed.

choices.english: they will immediately forget about the money
choices.why: ἐπιλανθάνομαι with genitive means to forget something; εὐθύς is 'immediately'; keeps the future tense.
rejected: they will straightway forget the money
they will at once be forgetful of the money

pass_b_english: They feed on dew alone, yet they contain the whole Muses within themselves. Hearing them, you would say that they were once human and have become cicadas.” So it is fitting to be content with present circumstances. And even if the tax collectors are troubling you, only sing to them, and they will immediately forget about the money.
